item.title: C/C++ Floating Point Rounding Techniques Beyond Basic Formatting
item.description:
“C/C++ Floating Point Rounding Techniques Beyond Basic Formatting”

When dealing with floating-point arithmetic in C or C++, achieving a specific rounded value for further computation presents nuances that go beyond simple output formatting. Relying solely on print formatting like %.2f only affects display, not the underlying numeric value. How do expert programmers manage truncation, rounding to nearest, or rounding up when precision is paramount?

What are the reliable techniques for manipulating floating-point values (float or double) to restrict them to a specific decimal precision for internal use, especially when accounting for the inherent limitations of binary floating-point representation?

item.title: C++ pow() Floating Point Issues When Casting to Integer
item.description:
“C++ pow() Floating Point Issues When Casting to Integer”

When utilizing the C++ pow(base, exponent) function, particularly with floating-point arguments or when the result is near an integer boundary, developers frequently encounter scenarios where casting the returned double to an int results in an unexpected lower integer value, such as obtaining 9999 instead of the expected 10000 when calculating $10^4$. Why does this subtle imprecision occur, and what are the most reliable methods to circumvent this behavior when integer results are required?
